population.definition: Sector Autónomo de Bissau (SAB), 3rd General Population and Housing Census 2009 (RGPH-2009), population corrected for post-census survey omission, including collective residents

source.title: RGPH-2009: Características socioculturais
source.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estatística, Guiné-Bissau (archived copy)

facts.claim: Work on building the Fortaleza de São José de Bissau began in 1765, a first step in creating a differentiated space on the island of Bissau.

source.title: Bissau (1765–1846): de factoría a enclave portugués
source.author: Carlos Franco Liberato
source.quote: el inicio de los trabajos de construcción de la Fortaleza de São José de Bissau en 1765

facts.claim: Only after the Bissau War of 1844 did the Portuguese obtain exclusive control of a small plot of land on the island, a real Portuguese enclave in the territory of the Papel people.

source.title: Bissau (1765–1846): de factoría a enclave portugués
source.author: Carlos Franco Liberato
source.quote: sólo con la Guerra de Bissau de 1844 es que los portugueses logran, finalmente, después de casi tres siglos y medio, obtener el control exclusivo sobre una parcela ínfima de tierra

facts.claim: Bissau was founded as a fort in 1765 and, after the slave trade declined in the early 19th century, became the chief commercial centre of Portuguese Guinea.

source.title: Portuguese Guinea - Early Developments
source.quote: Bissau, which had been founded as a fort in 1765, became the chief commercial center

facts.claim: On 19 December 1941 the capital of Portuguese Guinea was moved from Bolama to Bissau, where new infrastructure including a port had begun to be built.

source.title: Governo da Guiné-Bissau quer ver Bolama reconhecida como Património Mundial
source.quote: A 19 de Dezembro de 1941, a capital da Guiné Portuguesa foi transferida de Bolama para Bissau

facts.claim: The Sector Autónomo de Bissau is the Guinea-Bissau administrative unit alongside the eight regions.

source.title: RGPH-2009: Características socioculturais
source.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estatística, Guiné-Bissau (archived copy)
source.quote: está dividida em oito regiões - Bafatá, Biombo, Bolama, Cacheu, Gabú, Oio, Quinara e Tombali e mais o Sector Autónomo de Bissau (SAB)

facts.claim: In the 2009 census the largest share of the national population, 25.1 percent, lived in the Sector Autónomo de Bissau.

source.title: RGPH-2009: Características socioculturais
source.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estatística, Guiné-Bissau (archived copy)
source.quote: a maioria reside no SAB (25,1%)

facts.claim: In the Sector Autónomo de Bissau the Balanta (20.5%), Fula (18.0%), Papel (15.7%) and Mandinga peoples were the most numerous ethnic groups in 2009.

source.title: RGPH-2009: Características socioculturais
source.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estatística, Guiné-Bissau (archived copy)
source.quote: No Sector Autónomo de Bissau (SAB), os Balantas (20,5%), Fulas (18.0%), papeis (15,7%) e Mandingas representam as etnias com maior expressão

facts.claim: For a decade after independence, residents and business owners in Bissau Velho were required by law to repaint their building facades each December.

source.title: Crumbling architecture of former narco-state in Bissau
source.author: Ricci Shryock
source.quote: were required by law to repaint the facades of their buildings each December

facts.claim: Bandim, in Bissau, is considered the largest and best-supplied market in the country.

source.title: Mulheres bideiras (monografia)
source.publisher: Universidade da Integração Internacional da Lusofonia Afro-Brasileira (Unilab)
source.quote: é considerado o maior e mais bem fornecido mercado do país

timeline.claim: From the arrival of the Portuguese in the region in 1460, Portuguese and Papel peoples contended for power over the social spaces of the island of Bissau.

source.title: Bissau (1765–1846): de factoría a enclave portugués
source.author: Carlos Franco Liberato
source.quote: entre los años de 1460 y 1846, portugueses y papeis se enfrentaron en desigualdad de condiciones por el poder hegemónico sobre los espacios sociales de la isla de Bissau

timeline.claim: Construction of the Fortaleza de São José de Bissau began in 1765.

source.title: Bissau (1765–1846): de factoría a enclave portugués
source.author: Carlos Franco Liberato
source.quote: el inicio de los trabajos de construcción de la Fortaleza de São José de Bissau en 1765

timeline.claim: The Bissau War of 1844 allowed the Portuguese to build a real enclave on the island.

source.title: Bissau (1765–1846): de factoría a enclave portugués
source.author: Carlos Franco Liberato
source.quote: La construcción de fuertes portugueses en la factoría no fue capaz de cambiar este estado de cosas hasta la Guerra de Bissau de 1844

timeline.claim: Bolama became capital of the Portuguese colony on 18 March 1879, administered separately from Cape Verde.

source.title: Governo da Guiné-Bissau quer ver Bolama reconhecida como Património Mundial
source.quote: Bolama ascendeu a capital a 18 de Março de 1879

timeline.claim: The colonial capital was transferred from Bolama to Bissau on 19 December 1941.

source.title: Governo da Guiné-Bissau quer ver Bolama reconhecida como Património Mundial
source.quote: A 19 de Dezembro de 1941, a capital da Guiné Portuguesa foi transferida de Bolama para Bissau

timeline.claim: Guinea-Bissau became independent in 1974; for a decade afterwards Bissau Velho owners had to repaint facades each December.

source.title: Crumbling architecture of former narco-state in Bissau
source.author: Ricci Shryock
source.quote: For a decade after its independence in 1974

timeline.claim: The 2009 census corrected population of the Sector Autónomo de Bissau was 387,909.

source.title: RGPH-2009: Características socioculturais
source.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estatística, Guiné-Bissau (archived copy)

timeline.claim: The Bijagós Archipelago – Omatí Minhô became Guinea-Bissau's first World Heritage site.

source.title: Rainforests and reefs: new World Heritage sites signal conservation breakthroughs
source.quote: represents a major milestone for Guinea Bissau, as the country’s first World Heritage site

places.name: Coastal and Marine Ecosystems of the Bijagós Archipelago – Omatí Minhô
places.what: The Bijagós archipelago, off Bissau, was inscribed on the World Heritage List in 2025 as Guinea-Bissau's first site. It has 88 islands and islets and hosts green sea turtle nests and migrating birds.

source.title: Rainforests and reefs: new World Heritage sites signal conservation breakthroughs
source.quote: represents a major milestone for Guinea Bissau, as the country’s first World Heritage site
